## Short claims for proof steps

- **comp:shannon-lower-bound / Step 1**: Any circuit of size $s'<s$ can be padded with $s-s'$ gates of the form $g\wedge g$ after the output gate to obtain a circuit of size exactly $s$ computing the same function, so the number of functions computable by circuits of size at most $s$ is at most the number of circuits of size exactly $s$.
- **comp:shannon-lower-bound / Step 2**: The number of circuits of size exactly $s$ is at most $\bigl(3(n+2+s)^{2}\bigr)^{s}$, since each of the $s$ gates has at most $3$ types and at most $n+2+s$ choices for each of its (at most two) inputs.
- **comp:shannon-lower-bound / Step 3**: For $n\ge3$ one has $\log_{2}\bigl(\bigl(3(n+2+s)^{2}\bigr)^{s}\bigr)<2^{n}$, so fewer than $2^{2^{n}}$ functions are computable by circuits of size at most $s$, hence some function requires size greater than $2^{n}/(4n)$.
- **comp:deterministic-local-step / Step 1**: Defining $g$ on each window $(s_{-1},s_{0},s_{1},s_{2})$ by $g=s_{0}$ when the state symbol is halting or lies at position $l=2$ (or no state symbol is present), and by $g=g_{\tau}(s_{-1},s_{0},s_{1},s_{2})$ otherwise, yields a map $g\colon(C\cup\{\triangleright\})^{4}\to C$ with $c'_{j}=g(c_{j-1},c_{j},c_{j+1},c_{j+2})$ for all $1\le j\le m$, where $c'$ is the next configuration (or $c'=c$ if $c$ is halting).
- **comp:time-to-size / Step 1**: For each cell $(i,j)$ with $0\le i\le T$, $1\le j\le m$, the $k$ wires carry the encoding of the symbol at position $j$ of the configuration reached after $i$ steps of $M$ on $w$ (or of the halting configuration if $M$ has already halted), as proved by induction on $i$.
- **comp:time-to-size / Step 2**: The circuit has $O(T^{2})$ gates, since there are $(T+1)m=O(T^{2})$ cells and each cell uses a constant number $G$ of gates, so its size is $O(t(n)^{2})$.
- **comp:time-to-size / Step 3**: The circuit can be written out from $1^{n}$ in time polynomial in $t(n)$ whenever $t(n)$ is computable from $1^{n}$ in polynomial time in $t(n)$, because the same fixed gadgets are placed cell by cell.
- **comp:time-to-size / Step 4**: The output gate (the OR over all positions of the $T$-th row of the test 'the symbol is $q_{\mathrm{acc}}$') evaluates to $1$ exactly when $M$ accepts $w$ within $T$ steps, since $M$ halts within $T$ steps and the head stays within positions $1,\dots,m-1$.
- **comp:circuit-sat-complete / Step 1**: $\mathrm{CIRCUIT\text{-}SAT}\in\mathrm{NP}$: a satisfying input $x$ is a certificate, and evaluating the circuit gate by gate verifies it in polynomial time.
- **comp:circuit-sat-complete / Step 2**: For any $A\in\mathrm{NP}$ with polynomial-time verifier $V$, the map $w\mapsto C_{w}$ (the circuit obtained from the tableau circuit for $V$ on inputs of length $N$ by fixing the $w$-bits) is a polynomial-time reduction from $A$ to $\mathrm{CIRCUIT\text{-}SAT}$, because $C_{w}$ is satisfiable iff some certificate $c$ makes $V$ accept $\langle w,c\rangle$ iff $w\in A$.
- **comp:cook-levin-via-circuits / Step 1**: The Tseitin-style conjunction of the clauses $(z_{i}\leftrightarrow g_{i})$ (at most $3$ clauses per gate, $2$ for NOT) together with the output clause $(z_{s})$ is a 3CNF formula of size linear in the circuit whose satisfying assignments correspond one-to-one to the gate-value assignments, so it is satisfiable iff $C$ is.
